title: Spectra Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Use spectra to compare stars and infer composition, temperature and motion.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy stretch: spectral interpretation, classification and exam reasoning.
final_note: You can now build a star's full profile from one ribbon of light.

concepts.def: Dark or bright feature at a specific wavelength.
Strong in hot O and B stars.
Broad features in cool M stars from molecules.
Roman numeral (I supergiant to V main sequence).
Study of light split into its component wavelengths.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hydrogen lines peak in A-type stars (~10,000 K). Helium lines dominate hotter O/B stars. Cool M stars show molecular bands of TiO. Lines reveal both temperature and composition.
The Sun's classification G2V means spectral type G2 (yellow main sequence). A supergiant is class I, a giant III, a main sequence dwarf V. Lines' widths help distinguish luminosity classes.

For 'use the spectrum to describe the star': identify peak (gives T), strongest lines (gives composition and class), and any Doppler shift (gives radial motion). Always quote numerical values where given.
